## The honest CAPM test

### Tape 1 (SPAK)
OLS regression: r_SPAK = alpha + beta * r_SPY + eps

| Coefficient | Estimate | HAC t |
|---|---|---|
| **alpha (daily)** | **-14.538 bps/day** | **-1.925** |
| beta | 0.910 | — |
| R² | 0.333 | — |

Annualised alpha: **-30.69%/yr**. The HAC t-stat of -1.925 just misses the |t|=2 bar.
With only 1.92 years and high idiosyncratic vol (~45%/yr), the minimum detectable alpha
at |t|=2 is roughly ±22%/yr. The point estimate (-30.69%/yr) is extreme, but power is
limited at 483 daily observations.

**Raw excess return (SPAK - SPY): -14.946 bps/day, HAC t = -2.000** — this does clear
the bar, confirming the directional verdict even without beta-adjustment.

### Tape 2 (De-SPAC basket)
OLS regression: r_basket = alpha + beta * r_SPY + eps

| Coefficient | Estimate | HAC t |
|---|---|---|
| **alpha (daily)** | **-15.014 bps/day** | **-1.926** |
| beta | 2.023 | — |
| R² | 0.384 | — |

Annualised alpha: **-31.52%/yr**. Same pattern: enormous negative alpha, same t-stat
level. The higher beta (2.0) means the basket amplifies market losses and adds
catastrophic idiosyncratic losses on top.

## Structural dilution mechanics

Classic SPAC anatomy: sponsors receive ~20% of shares at a nominal price ($0 or near
zero), creating an immediate dilution of public shareholders at merger. Additionally:

- Warrants (often 1 per unit) dilute further if exercised
- SPAC units trade at ~$10 pre-merger (trust value); redemptions drain cash at merger
- Post-merger companies often projected forward revenues 5+ years; when growth missed,
  the collapse was swift
- SPAK had a ~0.45% ER added on top of the structural losses

These mechanics are not anomaly-based — they are architectural. The underperformance
is structural, not cyclical.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** HAC t(Jensen alpha) = -1.925 for SPAK (|t| < 2). The raw excess
  HAC t = -2.000 just reaches significance, but the window is too short (1.92 years)
  to certify the alpha formally. The direction — catastrophic underperformance — admits
  no ambiguity: -26% CAGR vs +10% CAGR, Sharpe -0.93 vs +0.63, max DD -62% vs -23%.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** SPAK CAGR -26.14% vs SPY +10.26%. An investor in SPAK
  over its full life lost ~36 percentage points per year versus simply owning the index.
  The 9-name basket over 4.56 years is even worse: -24% CAGR, -86% max drawdown.
- **SPACs: BUSTED.** The structural-dilution / promote / warrant mechanics transferred
  wealth from public investors to sponsors. The claim of "faster, smarter route to
  public markets" ignores the ~20% promote embedded in every SPAC deal.
